claim: Phone users can finger-drag vertical and horizontal UI lists while desktop users can wheel-scroll the hovered list without accidental child-button activation.
artifact_or_command: godot --headless --path project-a --script tools/run_mobile_scroll_input_tests.gd && godot --headless --path project-a --script tools/run_ui_smoke_tests.gd

assertions: Straight and slightly diagonal upward drags change vertical offset.
Dragging from a button does not activate it.
Straight and slightly diagonal left drags change horizontal offset.
Wheel changes a hovered vertical list by a deterministic step.
Wheel falls back to horizontal traversal for a horizontal-only runway.

environment.device: synthetic phone touch and desktop mouse

observation: MOBILE_SCROLL_INPUT_TESTS_OK and UI SMOKE TESTS PASS at revision 3b797a9.
inference: The global adapter now provides the requested phone drag and desktop wheel contract for both axes.
limitations: Physical-device momentum and browser overscroll feel still require human tuning.
